mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the previous three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 2% over six months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in CPIAUCSL below 1.5% and a cut in FEDFUNDS by at least 0.5% within a quarter signals an aggressive easing stance, lowering real interest rates and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% AND FEDFUNDS cut > 0.5% in same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS falling >0.5% for four consecutive months) signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
